topic.name: PD-L1
topic.short_description: Immune checkpoint protein - predictor for immunotherapy response
topic.seo_title: PD-L1 Cancer Research - Latest Studies & Findings | Your Cancer Breakthroughs
topic.seo_description: Explore PD-L1 biomarker research for cancer immunotherapy. Discover how this immune checkpoint protein predicts treatment response and advances personalized cancer care.
topic.seo_intro:
PD-L1 is an immune checkpoint protein that has become one of the most important biomarkers in modern cancer research. This protein sits on the surface of cancer cells and acts like a "brake" on the immune system, helping tumors evade detection and attack by the body's natural defenses. By understanding PD-L1 levels, researchers and oncologists can better predict which patients may respond to immunotherapy treatments, a category of drugs designed to release these brakes and allow the immune system to fight cancer more effectively.

Over the past decade, PD-L1 testing has transformed from a research curiosity into a standard diagnostic tool in cancer care. Measuring PD-L1 expression in tumors helps oncologists determine which patients might benefit most from checkpoint inhibitor drugs and which individuals may need alternative or combination treatment strategies. This biomarker-driven approach represents a shift toward precision medicine, where treatment decisions are based on individual tumor characteristics rather than a one-size-fits-all approach. Current research continues to explore how PD-L1 levels relate to treatment outcomes across different cancer types, how to best measure this biomarker, and whether PD-L1 status can help predict response to newer immunotherapy combinations.

On this page, you'll find summaries of the latest peer-reviewed studies examining PD-L1 as a cancer biomarker and diagnostic tool. These articles represent cutting-edge research from institutions worldwide focused on improving how we identify patients most likely to benefit from immunotherapy and advancing the field of personalized cancer treatment.

articles.title: Flexible Dual-Apt Scaffolds Reveal gPD-L1-sEVs in Breast Cancer.
articles.hook: Dual-aptamer scaffolds detect soluble PD-L1 in breast cancer serum
articles.summary: Researchers developed a highly sensitive test to detect a hidden form of PD-L1 protein in breast cancer patients, enabling better prediction of immunotherapy effectiveness.

articles.title: Programmed Death-Ligand 1 Expression Predicts Poor Prognosis in Patients With Early-Stage Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer Undergoing Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy.
articles.hook: High PD-L1 expression predicts poor outcomes in early-stage lung cancer after stereotactic body radiotherapy
articles.summary: High PD-L1 levels predict worse outcomes in early-stage lung cancer patients treated with radiation therapy.

articles.title: Official Title: A Phase 2 Study to Evaluate Zimberelimab (AB122) Combined With AB154 in Front-Line, PD-L1-High, Locally Advanced or Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
articles.hook: Zimberelimab plus AB154 shows efficacy in PD-L1-high lung cancer
articles.summary: A Phase 2 trial tests two immunotherapy drugs combined to treat advanced non-small cell lung cancer in patients with high PD-L1 expression.

articles.title: A Phase III, Multisite, Randomized, Double-Blind Trial of BNT327 in Combination With Chemotherapy Versus Placebo With Chemotherapy in Patients With Previously Untreated Locally Recurrent Inoperable or Metastatic TNBC Determined Ineligible for PD(L)1 Therapy Based on PD-L1 Negative Disease
articles.hook: BNT327 plus chemotherapy improves outcomes in PD-L1 negative triple-negative breast cancer
articles.summary: A trial tests whether BNT327 combined with chemotherapy improves outcomes in triple-negative breast cancer patients ineligible for standard immunotherapy.

articles.title: Age-Associated Targetable Genomic Alterations and PD-L1 Expression in 2509 Patients With Pulmonary Ground-Glass Opacities.

articles.summary: Cancer-supporting cells secrete CXCL11, which promotes nasopharyngeal carcinoma growth and immune evasion through a specific signaling pathway.

articles.title: Durvalumab and tremelimumab combination therapy achieved remarkable response in primary hepatic undifferentiated carcinoma with high PD-L1 expression.
articles.hook: Two immunotherapy drugs shrank rare liver cancer...
